title: Circular Ring Buffer with Read Pointers

argv: from ring.buffer import RingBuffer; b=RingBuffer(3); [b.write(i) for i in range(5)]; print(b.read(10)); print(b.read(10))

trajectory.text: No tests exist in the repo. Let me verify the fix works with a quick manual check.

trajectory.note: Fixed ring/buffer.py so write() advances the head pointer when the buffer is full (overwriting oldest data), while read() already correctly advances the read pointer without reading past the write pointer.
trajectory.text: The fix works correctly. Writing 0-4 into a capacity-3 buffer overwrites oldest data, so reading returns `[2, 3, 4]`, and subsequent reads return empty.

trajectory.note: Fixed ring/buffer.py: write() now advances the head pointer when the buffer is full so writing overwrites the oldest data, and read() correctly limits to size so it never reads past the write pointer.
trajectory.text:
The fix works correctly. Writing 0-4 into a capacity-3 buffer overwrites oldest data, so reading returns [2, 3, 4] (the last 3 items), and a second read returns empty since the read pointer advanced past the write pointer.

The bug is fixed: when the buffer is full, `write` now advances the head pointer to overwrite the oldest data, and `read` correctly limits reads to `self._size` so it never reads past the write pointer.

trajectory.note: Fixed ring/buffer.py: write() now advances the head pointer when the buffer is full so overwriting discards the oldest data, and read() correctly advances past the write pointer.
trajectory.text:
The fix works correctly. Writing 5 items into a capacity-3 buffer overwrites the oldest, so reading returns `[2, 3, 4]` (the last 3 written), and a second read returns empty since the read pointer advanced past the write pointer.

The bug was in the `write` method: when the buffer was full, it failed to advance the `_head` pointer, so overwriting the oldest data left the head pointing at stale data. The fix advances `_head` when overwriting.
